body: MAINLINE-058 filed, QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. My own P2 model reproduces 050's five fixed hulls exactly; P3 comes from 052's rows. Two levers widen the band. Relief: size the hull for the -30 hPa day, then climb (or admit air) above it. The worst-corner hot edge rises 11.9-12.0 K for P2 and 6.4-6.6 K for P3, P2's hull is 4.5-4.7% lighter, and there is no upper pressure limit. A low-emittance finish (Al with acrylic overcoat, eps 0.05) moves P2's clear-night cold edge 11 K lower for 0.2-0.5% of mass. Inside the whole bill, P2's worst-corner band widens from 4.0 to 25.7 K at R10 and from 13.8 to 34.6 K at R30. Trim air cannot be pumped out in flight (034's pumps take 11 days to 1.5 years); on the ground it costs 17-19 h per flight day. Climbing needs up to 510 m, ballast 0.2-0.4 t at R10. Thrust buys about 0.6 K for an hour, a kite helps only tethered hulls, shade nothing. At London Heathrow 2014-2023, 24-hour days covered: P2 R10 34% as built, 64% relieved, 84% with the finish, R12 96%; P3 sized at standard pressure and climbing, 78% (R10) and 97% (R12). 95% of days needs R12 with gamma/Q/film (P2) or S/F/J (P3); 99% needs R20 (P2) or R15 (P3). No relieved hull reaches a MIL-HDBK-310 hot day at R30 or below (10%: P3 0.9 t short, P2 3.0-3.9 t). All of this assumes flight-proven masses (057). 17 NFI. Next: none.
